experiment.name: phase1_traffic_volume
description: Does leakage scale with how much operand data moves, and with how far it
phase1_memory_replication established that operand movement leaks and
register-resident operands do not, and hinted that loads and stores are
roughly additive (0.21 + 0.32 ~ 0.51 W). That was three points at a fixed
traffic level. This sweeps two axes independently:
volume  1 / 2 / 4 / 8 loads per iteration, working set pinned in L1
depth   16K / 512K / 4M / 32M working set, loads pinned at 8
Sized against this part: L1d 48K and L2 1.25M per P-core, L3 24M shared.
With four victim threads the 4M variant totals 16M and still fits L3,
while 32M each must stream from DRAM. If leakage tracks bus capacitance,
the depth axis should matter more than the volume axis.
The driver now reports victim_bytes_per_s, so the watt differences can be
normalised to leakage per byte of operand traffic rather than compared
only by victim name -- the variants do not move data at equal rates.

runs.label: aa_control_dram
runs.comment: A/A on the heaviest-traffic victim; gates the whole sweep.
